classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the equal cable lengths, calculate the attachment height using Pythagoras’ theorem, then include the flag’s vertical dimension.

content.prompt: A flagpole is supported by two cables of equal length as shown below. The total length of the cables is 100 m. Each cable is attached to a point on level ground 40 m away from the foot of the flagpole. The dimensions of the flag are $1.2\text{ m}\times2.4\text{ m}$. Calculate the height to the top of the flag.

spec.description: Two cables meet the vertical pole at the lower edge of a rectangular flag. Ground anchors lie on opposite sides of the pole, each labelled 40 m from its foot. The flag is wider than it is high. Ordinary source blue outlines are rendered black in house style.
spec.mathematics: Each cable forms the hypotenuse of a right triangle with horizontal distance 40 m and a common vertical attachment height. The flag extends above the cable attachment.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry and the two 40 m labels are visible; calculated lengths are absent.

answer.worked:
Each cable has length $100\div2=50\text{ m}$. Let $h$ be the height of the cable attachment, in metres.

$$\begin{align*}h^2+40^2&=50^2\\h^2+1600&=2500\\h^2&=2500-1600\\h^2&=900\\h&=30\end{align*}$$

The flag is wider than it is high, so its vertical dimension is $1.2\text{ m}$.

$$\text{Height to the top of the flag}=30+1.2=31.2\text{ m}.$$
